tasks.short: Check assignments and answer keys for errors, collect student questions that point to errors, write the error report, and send it to the instructor.

steps.what: Teaching assistant checks assignments and answer keys for errors or problems
Students post suspected errors in the tagged course forum thread
Teaching assistant collects student questions that point to errors
Teaching assistant writes the error report for the instructor
Teaching assistant reads the report before sending: each error is real, the question and proposed fix are right, and it goes to the instructor of this course
Teaching assistant sends the report to the instructor: by e-mail today, by one release from the course system after the change

tasks.design: For numeric questions, a script recomputes the answer key from the question data, so wrong keys show before marking. Students report suspected errors in a tagged thread on the course forum ({LMS}), which groups reports per question instead of separate e-mails. Error reports use a short form with question, problem and proposed fix; the teaching assistant writes and checks each report and sends it once to the instructor. Judging whether something is an error stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Keys were checked by hand and student reports came by separate e-mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Course forums group posts by tag; scripts can recompute numeric keys.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous wording is not caught by a script.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that many wrong answers point to an unclear question, not weak students.

reach.learn: Whether errors are fixed before grading.

evidence.claim: Course forums can group posts by tag; scripts can recompute numeric answer keys.

assumptions: Boundary: from the assignment set to the instructor notified; the instructor's fix is outside.
Input contract: question data in the course system; fallback is checking by hand and e-mail.
Students post on the forum in about the time an e-mail took; no added student time.
Judging errors stays with the assistant. s3 keeps 85: the form gives the fields, but describing each problem and fix is still written. Students' forum posts (s1b) replace their e-mails.
research_questions: Are errors found before grading more often?

incremental.description: Teaching assistant keeps the key-check script in step with new questions.

approvals.approved_version: The error report with each question, problem and proposed fix exactly as checked by the teaching assistant in s3b, sent once to this course's instructor; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few numeric questions, so the key-check script finds little (s1 90) (22.2); high: large courses with many numeric assignments (31.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work through the laboratory project before students do, note problems and timing, write modification proposals, send them to the instructor, and update the lab manual.

steps.what: Teaching assistant completes laboratory projects prior to assigning them to students
Teaching assistant notes problems and timing: in a notebook today, in the trial form after the change
Teaching assistant writes proposals so needed modifications can be made
Teaching assistant reads the proposal before sending: each change follows from the trial notes and says which step and why
Teaching assistant sends the proposal to the instructor: by e-mail today, by one share in the course space after the change
Teaching assistant updates the lab manual after the instructor agrees

tasks.design: Trial notes go into a form attached to the lab project in the shared course space ({DOCS}) with fields for step, problem, time taken and photos, so notes are not copied from a notebook into the proposal; writing the notes keeps its time. The lab manual is a shared document with version history, so agreed changes are made in one place. Doing the trial and proposing changes stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were kept in paper notebooks and the manual existed in several copies.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared course spaces hold forms and versioned manuals.
tasks.still_hard: A trial by an expert does not show where students will struggle.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which step will confuse a first-year student.

reach.learn: Whether lab sessions run on time.

evidence.claim: Shared course spaces can hold forms and versioned manuals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lab project to the manual updated; lab sessions are outside.
Input contract: manuals kept in the shared space; fallback is notebooks and copies.

Trialling and writing trial notes keep their full time; notes are a first record. s3 keeps 80 because notes are no longer copied into the proposal. s5 keeps 80: version history ends managing copies, but editing the manual stays.
The instructor's time does not change.
research_questions: Do fewer problems come up in student sessions?

incremental.description: Teaching assistant sets up the trial form for each project.

approvals.approved_version: The modification proposal exactly as checked by the teaching assistant in s3b, sent once to the lab project's instructor; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few changes per project, so little copying is saved (s3 95) (4.8); high: new projects with many changes (7.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare experiments and equipment, collect samples and measurements, record data, label and store samples, and discuss progress with the researcher.

steps.what: Teaching assistant prepares experiments and equipment to assist faculty with laboratory research
Teaching assistant collects samples and measurements in the lab or field
Teaching assistant records data in a paper lab notebook and a spreadsheet
Teaching assistant labels samples
Teaching assistant stores samples in the freezer or cabinet
Teaching assistant discusses progress with the researcher

tasks.design: An electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}) takes instrument exports directly and holds field entries made on a tablet, so data are not copied from paper into spreadsheets. It prints barcode labels for samples, linked to their data. Preparing experiments, collecting samples and discussing progress stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were written on paper and copied into spreadsheets; labels were handwritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic lab notebooks import instrument data and print sample labels.
tasks.still_hard: Field work in bad weather makes tablet entry awkward.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a sample that looks contaminated.

reach.learn: Whether data arrive clean and linked to samples.

evidence.claim: Electronic lab notebooks can import instrument data and print sample labels.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research plan to progress discussed; analysis is outside.
Input contract: instruments that export data; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Lab and field work do not change.
The researcher's time does not change.
Storing samples (s5) keeps its full time; only labelling (s4) is priced, at what printing barcode labels removes compared with handwriting them.

incremental.description: Teaching assistant sets up notebook templates per experiment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few instruments export, so most data are still typed (s3 70) (8.0); high: most measurements come from instrument exports (14.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate laboratory equipment to students, watch them and enforce laboratory rules, and check that each student has completed the safety instruction.

steps.what: Students complete the online safety module and quiz before their first session
Teaching assistant demonstrates use of laboratory equipment
Teaching assistant enforces laboratory rules
Teaching assistant checks paper safety sign-offs at the lab door

tasks.design: Students complete a short online safety module and quiz in the learning environment ({LMS}) before their first session, and the session list shows who has passed, replacing paper sign-offs checked at the door. Demonstrating equipment and enforcing rules in the lab stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety sign-offs were paper forms checked one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments run short modules and show completion on session lists.
tasks.still_hard: Passing a quiz does not mean a student works safely.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a student before a careless move with a hot plate.

reach.learn: Whether every student is instructed before access.

evidence.claim: Learning environments can run safety modules and show completion on session lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lab session to rules enforced; lab design is outside.
Input contract: module kept by the lab manager; fallback is paper sign-offs.
Students spend a little time on the module; priced as customer time.
Demonstrating and enforcing do not change.

incremental.description: Teaching assistant follows up students who have not passed the module.
Students take the online safety module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many students skip the module and sign paper at the door (s3 60) (3.5); high: nearly all pass the module first (6.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teaching assistant keeps trialling labs, assisting research, demonstrating and enforcing rules; hand checks, paper notebooks and sign-off forms shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with more time helping students in the lab.
